paragraphs.text: God had at first set him over the nations and over the kingdoms - as a plenipotentiary - "to root out and to pull down, and to destroy and to throw down, to build and to plant." {Jer 1:10} This power of his the prophet had put forth and exercised against his own nation of the Jews, whom he had doomed to destruction, and lived to see execution done accordtngly.
paragraphs.anchor: The word of the Lord which came to Jeremiah against the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: Now he takes their enemies, the neighbour nations, to do, telling them individually what they shall trust to. And this indeed the prophet had done before in part, and in fewer words, under the type of a cup of wine to be divided among and drunk up by the nations, {Jer 25:15-33} but here to the end of Jer 51:1-64. more plainly and plentifully.

Isaiah had done the same in effect (Isa 13:1-22; Isa 14:1-32; Isa 15:1-9; Isa 16:1-14; Isa 17:1-14; Isa 18:1-7; Isa 19:1-25; Isa 20:1-6; Isa 21:1-17; Isa 22:1-25; Isa 23:1-18; Isa 24:1-23), Ezekiel also, from Eze 25:1-17; Eze 26:1-21; Eze 27:1-36; Eze 28:1-26; Eze 29:1-21; Eze 30:1-26; Eze 31:1-18; Eze 32:1-32; Eze 33:1-33, that by the mouth of three such witnesses every word might stand, and this burden of the nations might be confirmed.

Jeremiah beginneth fitly with the Egyptians, who besides the old enmity, had lately slain good King Josiah, with whom died all the prosperity of the Jewish people, who were thenceforth known, as the Thebans also were after the death of their Epaminondas, only by their overthrows and calamities.
First, That the Jews might not rely on that broken reed, as they did to their ruin, because they would never be warned.
paragraphs.anchor: Against Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Who had beaten Nebuchadnezzar Priscus at Carchemish, and gotten all the country from Egypt to Euphrates; but was afterwards himself beaten out again, by Nebuchadnessar II, surnamed Magnus, in the first year of his reign, which was the fourth year of Jehoiakim, who also was glad to become his tributary. {a} Now this overthrow of the Egyptian, who was driven out of all Syria, as far as Pelusium, by the Babylonian, is here foretold.
paragraphs.anchor: Against the army of Pharaohnecho.

paragraphs.text: {a} Joseph., lib. x. cap. 7.

So Pharaoh is brought in bespeaking his forces, when he was going to fight against Nebuchadnezzar. Or so the prophet bespeaketh the Egyptians ironically, {a} and by way of scoff; q.d., Do so, but all shall be to no purpose, {b} See the like Isa 8:9. Congregamini et vincemini. We are assembled and will be conquered. Yea, though upon Pharaoh’s shield should be the same inscription that was once upon Agamemnon’s, This is the terror of all mortal wights. {c}
paragraphs.anchor: Order ye the buckler and shield.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hypotuposis ironica.
{b} State galeati, loricati, lanceati: sed frustra.
{c} Oυτος μεν φσβος εστι βροτων. - Pausan.

Those warlike creatures, but yet vain things for safety. {Psa 33:17 Pro 21:31} Egypt was famous for the best horses; {Deu 17:16 1Ki 10:26; 1Ki 10:28} but the Lord delighteth not in the strength of a horse, &c. {Psa 147:10-11}
paragraphs.anchor: Harness the horses.

paragraphs.text: Surprised with a panic terror.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore have I seen them dismayed?

paragraphs.text: Heb., Fled to flight.
paragraphs.anchor: And are fled apace.

paragraphs.text: A proverbial form. {Jer 6:25}
paragraphs.anchor: For fear was round about.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Think to save themselves by flight.
paragraphs.anchor: Let not the swift fly away

paragraphs.text: i.e., Think to save himself by his might, be he never so stout hearted.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor the mighty man escape

paragraphs.text: i.e., Toward Carchemish, the stage of the war, where Pharaohnecho had beaten Nebuchadnezzar the elder, and is now beaten in the same place by Nebuchadnezzar the younger, alterna victoria in another victory. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Toward the north

paragraphs.text: {a} Herod., lib. ii., αλλοπροσαλλος.
Pharaoh with his forces is here notably described, vivo sermonum colore, and compared to an impetuous river, that threateneth to overflow and swallow up all. See Isa 8:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Who is this that cometh up like a flood?

paragraphs.text: Like the Nile. The Egyptians were an ancient, proud, luxurious people.
paragraphs.anchor: Egypt riseth up like a flood.

paragraphs.text: See the like vain vaunts of this proud people, Exo 15:9-10.
paragraphs.anchor: And he saith, I will go up and cover the earth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Ye horsemen, all the cavalry of Egypt. {as Exo 14:7}
paragraphs.anchor: Come up, ye horses

paragraphs.text: Or, Bestir yourselves as if ye were wild or mad: instar furiarum discurrite per campos.
paragraphs.anchor: And rage.

paragraphs.text: The Africans that were confederates and auxiliaries to the Egyptians.
paragraphs.anchor: The Ethiopians and the Lybians.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 34:5-8.
paragraphs.anchor: For this is the day of the Lord God of hosts.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 8:22 cf. Gen 37:25; q.d., Thy calamity is no less incurable than ignominious.
paragraphs.anchor: Go up unto Gilead, and take balm.

paragraphs.text: Of the shameful defeat given thee; so that thou who wast once a terror to them art now a scorn.
paragraphs.anchor: The nations have heard of thy shame.

paragraphs.text: And this is the sum of the talk that goeth of thee.
paragraphs.anchor: For the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty.

paragraphs.text: Another prophecy, but against Egypt also. God had yet a further quarrel to that country for the death of good Josiah; their delivering up Uriah, God’s faithful servant, to the sword of Jehoiakim; their idolatry, pride, perfidy, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: The word that the Lord spake.

paragraphs.text: How Nebuchadnezzar … should come and smite the land of Egypt.] In the twentieth-fifth year of his reign, as Jeremiah also had set forth by a sign. {Jer 44:30}
See Jer 44:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Publish in Noph, and in Tahpanhes.

paragraphs.text: Egypt was no whit amended by the former discomfiture at Carchemish; therefore is now wholly subdued by the Babylonian conqueror, about three and twenty years after. And the like befell the Greek empire, overturned by the Turks.
paragraphs.anchor: For the sword shall devour roundabout thee.

paragraphs.text: He struck a panic terror into them; and then no wonder that men flee at the noise of a shaken leaf.
paragraphs.anchor: They stood not, because the Lord did drive them.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 46:12. In a confused flight it is wont so to be.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, one fell upon another.

paragraphs.text: The auxiliary and stipendiary soldiers said so, when once they saw that there was no good to be done for the Egyptians, Nebuchadnezzar having so wasted all.
paragraphs.anchor: And they said.

paragraphs.text: {a} A mere flash, one that vaunteth and vapoureth, and that is all. So of Charles VIII, King of France, Guicciardini saith, that in his expedition to Naples he came into the field like thunder and lightning, but went out like a snuff; more than a man at first, and less than a woman at last.
paragraphs.anchor: Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise

paragraphs.text: He let slip his best opportunity, which, in giving battle, is sometimes the loss of all. Charles, King of Sicily and Jerusalem, was for this fault called Carolus Cunctator, i.e., The Delayer.
paragraphs.anchor: He hath passed the time appointed.

paragraphs.text: {a} Strepitus est.
Formula iurandi elliptica, et Deo propria. Let none presume to swear in that sort.
paragraphs.anchor: As I live.

paragraphs.text: As Tabor surmounts and commandeth the little hills round about it, and Carmel the adjoining sea, over which it hangeth a promontory, so shall Nebuchadnezzar come into Egypt and subdue the whole country.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely as Tabor is among the mountains.

paragraphs.text: But not likely to dwell long there.
paragraphs.anchor: O thou daughter dwelling in Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Make thee instruments or implements of captivity. Sarcinis reculisque collectis, prepare to be packing.
paragraphs.anchor: Furnish thyself to go into captivity.

paragraphs.text: Vitula elegans, a trim bullock; {a} worshipping Apis the bull and Mnevis the cow, and unaccustomed to the yoke of subjection, {as Hos 10:11} but I shall bring her to it.
paragraphs.anchor: Egypt is like a very fair heifer.

paragraphs.text: Or, Excision from the north cometh, cometh, certo, cito, penitus venit {Eze 7:6} There come those that shall cut up this fair heifer or fat calf.
paragraphs.anchor: Destruction cometh.

paragraphs.text: {a} Iuvenca petulca.

Heb., Bullocks of the stall, not like to do much good service in respect of their luxury and petulancy; fat Eglon had but sluggish soldiers. Campania with her delicacies marred Hannibal’s forces. These mercenaries carried themselves as if hired non ad militiam sed saginam. not to fight, but to fat themselves
paragraphs.anchor: Also her hired men in the midst of her like fatted bullocks.

paragraphs.text: The voice thereof (of Egypt) shall go like a serpent.] {a} Submissa voce loquetur. She shall hiss and whisper, as being daunted and damped, scarce able to mutter or utter aught for fear. {Isa 29:4}
{a} Vox trepida et prae metu instar serpentum stridula.
i.e., Her many cities. Herodotus telleth of one thousand and twenty cities that were in the land of Egypt in the days of King Amasis.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall cut down her forest

paragraphs.text: The Babylonian sellers are; and those many hands will make light work. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Because they are more than the grasshoppers.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. ii.; Diodor., lib. i. cap. 31.
This is, in plain terms, the sum of all that had been said before. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded.

paragraphs.text: {a} Subiungit epiphonema.
And shall he say and not do? {Num 23:19} Shall the word of God be broken {Joh 10:35}
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saith.

paragraphs.text: Called populous No, {Nah 3:8} populous as Nineveh; so Galilee of the Gentiles. Some render it nourishing No. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I will punish the multitude of No.

paragraphs.text: Here Calvin conjectureth that Pharaoh had made many of his princes kings for his greater magnificence; but this came down soon after. A bulging wall is near unto a downfall.
paragraphs.anchor: And their kings.

paragraphs.text: Hophra. {Jer 44:30}
paragraphs.anchor: And Pharaoh.

paragraphs.text: As the Jews in Egypt did.
paragraphs.anchor: And all them that trust in him.

paragraphs.text: Forty years after {Eze 29:13} - sc., in the days of Amasis, whom Cambyses the Persian conquered, after which it remained subject to the Persian monarchs one hundred and fifty years, saith Eusebius, being but a base and tributary kingdom.
paragraphs.anchor: And afterward it shall be inhabited.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hodie dicitur Alexandria. Today it is called Alexandria.
If Egypt find so much favour, {as Jer 46:26} what mayest not thou hope for? See the same, Jer 30:10.
paragraphs.anchor: But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 30:11.
paragraphs.anchor: Fear thou not, O Jacob, &c.

paragraphs.text: God dealeth much otherwise with his own people than he doth with unbelievers, whose prosperity, as it is full of thorns, so their adversity is but a foretaste of eternal torment; whereas "all things," even afflictions also, "work together for good to them that love God."
paragraphs.anchor: But correct thee in measure, &c.
